message.content:
Sure! To pull **only** the `id` and `context` fields from the CAA records for `sample2.com`, you’ll want to use the API’s *field selection* (sometimes called “projection” or “select”) feature so that the server returns just what you need instead of the full record payload.

Below is a generic example that shows the pattern you’d follow. Replace the placeholder values (`https://api.yourdnsprovider.com`) with your provider’s real base URL.

---

### 1. Build the Request URL

```
GET https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records
    ?type=CAA          # Filter to only CAA records
    &fields=id,context # Tell the API to return only these two fields
```

> **Note:**  
> • Some APIs use `select=` instead of `fields=` – e.g., `?select=id,context`.  
> • If the API doesn’t support field selection, you’ll have to fetch the full records and trim them client‑side.

### 2. Add Authentication

Most DNS‑management APIs expect the API key in an Authorization header:

```http
Authorization: Bearer secret567
```

If your provider expects the key in a query parameter or a custom header, adjust accordingly.

### 3. Full Example (curl)

```bash
curl -X GET \
     "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567"
```

### 4. Expected Response

A typical JSON response would look like this:

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "id": "rec12345",
      "context": { /* whatever context data your provider supplies */ }
    },
    {
      "id": "rec67890",
      "context": { /* ... */ }
    }
  ]
}
```

Only the `id` and `context` keys appear; everything else is omitted.

---

#### Quick Checklist

| Step | What to Verify |
|------|----------------|
| Base URL | Is `https://api.yourdnsprovider.com` correct? |
| Endpoint Path | Does `/v1/domains/{domain}/records` match your provider’s spec? |
| Query Params | Do they use `type=` and `fields=` (or `select=`)? |
| Auth Header | Is `Bearer` the right scheme? |

Once you confirm those details, you’re good to go. Happy querying!
